directions.hypothesis: The game kicks off at 8:15 PM EST on Thursday, Nov 19. Several outlets argue that Houston (3-6) is overpriced as a double-digit favorite. Their reasons: the Texans' poor record as a favorite, a six-game ATS losing streak at home, the Colts covering five of the last seven meetings, and linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair going on IR. This counts as one lead, not three separate ones. Published lines ranged from +10.5 to +13.5, so the number has moved.
directions.question: What is the current spread? Does the +10.5 to +13.5 range offered in the pieces still exist? And do Indianapolis's injured corners or its protection problems point to a lopsided Houston win?

directions.hypothesis: Houston has gone Over in 6 of 9 games, and its last four games each reached at least 48 points. Indianapolis ranks 28th in points allowed. The Covers AI model projects 47 total points. The total opened at 43.5 and moved to 44.5.
directions.question: Has the total risen past 44.5? Would a Houston blowout, or the Colts' protection problems stalling their offense, keep Indianapolis from scoring its share?

directions.hypothesis: Houston's running game is thin: Woody Marks is in concussion protocol and David Montgomery has a groin injury. Colts starting corners Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward are both questionable. Stroud has completed at least 21 passes in three of his four home starts. The analyst cites projections of 19.7 to 22.5 completions.
directions.question: Will Gardner and Ward play? And if Houston builds a big lead, will that cut Stroud's late-game passing volume?

directions.hypothesis: Stroud averages 35.6 pass attempts per game, and Houston's running game has added little. This was one leg of a combo pick, not a standalone pick.
directions.question: If Montgomery plays a full workload and Houston leads by double digits, does Stroud's attempt count drop below his season average?

directions.hypothesis: Collins drew a season-high 16 targets last week and caught 9 passes. He has at least five catches in each of his last four games against the Colts. Indianapolis plays a lot of man coverage and may be missing its top corners.
directions.question: Are Gardner and Ward ruled out or active? Is Collins dealing with any limitation on the short week?

directions.hypothesis: Taylor has drawn 14 targets over the last three games and is still Indianapolis's third-down back. The Colts' receiving group is depleted. The analyst expects a game script that favors passing for the big underdog. Some models have him near 16 yards, though most are above 20.
directions.question: Will rookie Seth McGowan's growing snap share, including on passing downs, cap how many routes Taylor runs?

directions.hypothesis: As a big underdog, Indianapolis should be forced to pass. Houston has allowed many explosive pass plays. VSiN's OptaAI projects about 189 yards. A Covers projection table showed a higher number, but that page's date stamp looks inconsistent.
directions.question: Jones struggled last week. Will Indianapolis's depleted receiving corps and protection problems hold down his efficiency even if he throws a lot?

directions.hypothesis: With Woody Marks in concussion protocol, Montgomery may get most of the carries. Indianapolis has allowed 4.88 yards per carry and has been weak against the run recently. This lead conflicts with the Stroud passing-volume leads, so both can't be right.
directions.question: How limited is Montgomery by his groin injury, and how will the carries split if Marks is ruled out?
directions.published_line: Montgomery rushing yards, in play up to 54+

directions.hypothesis: Hutchinson has scored in three straight games, drew nine targets last week, and has had a red-zone target in four straight games. A Covers pick listed him Over 39.5 receiving yards, and a lower 32.5 line was quoted elsewhere.
directions.question: Is his recent target share stable with Collins healthy, or was it a one-off from Houston throwing heavily against Cleveland?
